Advogato Flow

Advogato admitted an account when one unit of integer network flow could reach it from a few trusted seeds, through a web of certifications whose capacity shrinks with distance. Draw a graph, pick seeds, edit the schedule, and step through the computation — the explanation on the right always describes the state you are looking at.

Every account at every threshold

Account Seed Distance Capacity c(v) Consumed Forwarded Result Apprentice Journeyer Master Reported level

Distance, capacity, consumed and forwarded are for the selected threshold. "Reported level" is the highest threshold at which the account was accepted, which is what tmetric_run records: it runs the metric once per level and overwrites the level upward.

How the computation works
  1. Choose a certification threshold — Apprentice, Journeyer or Master. Keep only the certifications at that level or higher. In tmetric_run a certification at level L is added to the flow graphs of every level 1 … L, so the Master graph is a subgraph of the Journeyer graph, which is a subgraph of the Apprentice graph.
  2. Connect a synthetic source — a node named -, created first so it has index 0 — to every trusted seed. The reference treats it like any other node: it is at distance 0, it gets caps[0], and one of those units is spent on its own sink edge, so at most caps[0] − 1 real accounts can ever be accepted.
  3. Breadth-first search from the source assigns every reachable node a distance d and a capacity c(v) = caps[d]; past the end of the schedule the last entry persists. A node with no certification path from a seed is never reached, keeps capacity −1, and receives no trust at all.
  4. Split every node v into vin and vout, and add three kinds of edge: vin → vout with capacity c(v) − 1; vin → shared sink with capacity 1; and, for every certification u → v, uout → vin with no capacity limit. The one unit a node may send to the sink is the unit that admits it; the other c(v) − 1 units are all it can ever forward. In net_flow_max_flow this is the TWEAK: capacity[i]-- plus a per-node node_sink ∈ {0, 1}.
  5. Compute an integer maximum flow from the source to the shared sink. The reference finds augmenting paths by breadth-first search over the residual graph (net_flow_augment): forward along certifications, through a node if it still has forwarding capacity, and backwards along any edge that already carries flow, which is how a unit gets re-routed to make room for another. The first in-node the search reaches whose sink edge is empty gets the next unit.
  6. Accept every account whose sink edge carries one unit. Every accepted account consumed exactly one unit; every unit that reached the sink admitted exactly one account. The total flow is the number of accepted accounts, counting the source.
  7. Repeat for each threshold and report, for every account, the highest level at which it was accepted. The three runs are independent maximum flows, so an account can in principle be accepted at Master and lose a tie at Journeyer; the reference still reports Master, because it overwrites the level upward.

Modeling choices and simplifications
  • Kept from the reference: the synthetic source as node 0 with its own reserved unit; capacity indexed by BFS distance with the last schedule entry persisting; the in/out split with c(v) − 1 on the through-edge and 1 on the sink edge; breadth-first augmenting paths visited in the same order as net_flow_augment; the per-level run with the highest accepting level reported; dropping self-certifications the way net_flow_init_graph drops self-edges.
  • Simplified: the reference first builds a greedy tree (net_flow_assign_tree) and starts the flow from it before augmenting; this simulator starts from zero flow. The maximum flow value is the same either way. What can differ is which of several equally valid accepted sets comes out, because a maximum flow is not unique — and no tie-break is a trust judgement. Likewise, the order in which accounts and certifications were created is the traversal order here (the reference reads accounts from a directory), so identical inputs always give identical results, but the particular winners of a tie are an artefact of order.
  • Schedule entries must be ≥ 1. The reference reads its schedule up to the first zero, so a zero cannot appear inside it; a capacity of 1 is "may be accepted, forwards nothing".
  • Labels are not inputs. Scenario accounts marked "fake", "bad" or "confused" are drawn that way for the reader. The metric sees only accounts, certifications and seeds, and never which accounts are malicious.
  • Out of scope: Advogato's separate diary-rating system, which ranked diary entries with a different computation, is not modelled here. Neither is the reference's duplicate-edge handling (a profile holds one certification per subject, and the editor here does the same).

Compared with EigenTrust
Advogato (Levien)EigenTrust (Kamvar, Schlosser, Garcia-Molina)
OutputAn integer admission set: each account is in or out, once per level.A continuous reputation vector t summing to 1; accounts are ranked.
MechanismMaximum flow through capacities that fall with distance from the seeds.Power iteration of normalised local trust, mixed with pre-trusted peers.
FormulaAccept v iff the sink edge of vin carries 1 unit in a max flow.tnext = (1 − α) C⊤ t + α p
Role of the seedsThe source feeds them; capacity is a function of distance from them.The pre-trust vector p, uniform over the seeds; a peer that trusts nobody defers to p.
What a cluster of fakes getsAt most the units that cross the cut into the cluster — a count.The share of score that flows in, redistributed among its members — a fraction.

Same graph, same threshold, same seeds as pre-trusted peers

AccountEigenTrust scoreAdvogato result

Here every certification at or above the threshold is a local trust value of 1, normalised per certifier. α is left open in the paper; 0.15 is this page's default. Advogato's diary-rating system is a different computation and is outside this simulator's scope.

Sources
  • tmetric.c — mod_virgule's certification graph and per-level runs: the source node -, seeds, thresholds, and the highest-level report.
  • net_flow.c — capacity assignment by breadth-first search, the in/out split (TWEAK), and the augmenting-path maximum flow.
  • The EigenTrust Algorithm for Reputation Management in P2P Networks — Kamvar, Schlosser and Garcia-Molina, WWW 2003.
  • Jesse Ruderman, "Advogato's trust metric is not attack-resistant" (2005) — the distance-shortening attack behind the fourth scenario.
  • mod_virgule (Raph branch) — the whole Advogato code base, GPL.
